title: The duties of adults (mukallaf)
intro: Af‘al al-mukallafin: the eight kinds of rulings that cover everything an adult Muslim does.

learn.html: Af‘al al-mukallafin are the rules of the Shari‘ah for every Muslim man and woman who is adult and of sound mind. A person these duties apply to is called a mukallaf.
These rules cover the whole life of a person and of the community, so there is no action people do that is outside them. Af‘al al-mukallafin are divided into eight rulings:

learn.title: Fard
learn.html:
Fard are religious duties that Allah (SWT) strictly commanded to adult Muslims of sound mind. They are divided into:
• Fard ‘ayn – strict personal duties that every individual must do: the Kalimat ash-Shahadah, Salah, fasting, zakah and Hajj.
• Fard kifayah – strict duties of the community: if one group of Muslims does them, the others are freed from the duty. For example, the janazah prayer, or building things the community really needs – a mosque, a school, a hospital.

learn.title: Wajib
learn.html: Wajib are religious duties commanded by Allah (SWT), but not as strictly as fard. Examples are the duties Muslims do on the days of Eid: the Eid prayer, the Qurbani, saying the takbirs and giving sadaqat al-fitr.

learn.title: Haram
learn.html: Haram are things Allah (SWT) strictly forbade. Among them: drinking alcohol, eating pork and anything made from it, stealing, lying, zina (relations outside marriage), backbiting, gambling, drugs and so on.

A person who does not keep to the rules of fard, haram and wajib is a great sinner. But a person who denies a fard or a haram stops being a Muslim, and if they want to be a Muslim again they must say the Kalimat ash-Shahadah and make tawbah (repentance).
Sunnah is everything the Prophet Muhammad (SAW) said, did or recommended in any way. It is divided into:

items: Sunnah mu’akkadah – things the Prophet (SAW) did regularly and did not leave out, except in special situations. For example: the adhan and iqamah, praying in jama‘ah, and the sunnah prayers of Fajr, Dhuhr, Maghrib and Isha. Whoever does them benefits in this world and is rewarded in the next; whoever does not do them deserves blame.

Sunnah ghayr mu’akkadah – things the Prophet (SAW) did but sometimes left out, like the sunnah of Asr and of Isha (before the fard), and fasting on Mondays and Thursdays. Whoever does them is rewarded; whoever does not is not sinful.

Sunnah kifayah – things the Prophet (SAW) recommended to the community, which one or more people can do on behalf of the others, for example staying in the mosque in i‘tikaf for worship in the last ten days of Ramadan.

learn.title: Mustahab
learn.html: Mustahab are things that are good to do and that the Prophet (SAW) did from time to time. Examples: drying ourselves with a clean towel after wudu, praying nafl prayers, and so on.

learn.title: Makruh
learn.html:
Makruh are things that are disliked or ugly to do, but not clearly forbidden. They are divided into:
• Makruh tahrimi – close to haram and against wajib, so they are forbidden to do. Their prohibition is not as strong as haram, but there is a punishment for them. For example: hoarding food in a time of shortage to sell it at a higher price, eating or drinking from gold or silver dishes, a man sleeping on silk bedding, spreading gossip (“he said, she said”), asking pointless questions.
• Makruh tanzihi – not nice to do and against the Sunnah, so we should avoid them. For example: talking during the adhan and iqamah, eating with the left hand, entering the mosque with the left foot.

learn.title: Mubah
learn.html: Mubah are actions that are neither commanded nor forbidden – each person is free to choose, so they are allowed. If we do them, we are neither rewarded nor punished: for example, going for a walk or resting in our free time.

learn.title: Mufsid
learn.html:
Mufsid are things that spoil (break) acts of worship or duties:
• of wudu – flowing blood, sleeping, etc.;
• of Salah – speaking or laughing during the prayer, etc.;
• of fasting – eating or drinking on purpose during the fast, etc.;
• of Hajj – missing the standing at Arafah, etc.

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: Whoever does fard, wajib, sunnah or mustahab will be rewarded. Whoever does haram will be punished. Whoever does makruh things is left without reward. Whoever does mubah has neither punishment nor reward. Whoever does a mufsid has done wrong. These duties apply only to Muslims who are adult and of sound mind – nothing is prescribed for a young child or for a non-Muslim.

practice.title: Match the ruling and its meaning
pairs: Commanded, but less strictly than fard
Good to do, the Prophet (SAW) did it sometimes

practice.title: True or false?
practice.prompt: Sort each sentence from your book: true or false?

items.text: Fard kifayah is a duty of the community.
Mustahab are things the Prophet (SAW) did.
Mufsid are things that are only disliked to do.
Makruh tahrimi is close to halal.
The fard of Isha is a sunnah mu’akkadah.
Missing the sa‘y is the mufsid of Hajj.

practice.title: Fard ‘ayn
practice.prompt: Tap every fard ‘ayn – a duty every single Muslim must do – then tap Check.

options.why: The janazah prayer is fard kifayah – if a group does it, the others are freed.
The Qurbani is wajib, one of the duties of Eid.
